title: Pulse credits: periodic micro-allowances and SQ streamlining to improve PLG conversion
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Run a controlled experiment that issues small periodic 'pulse' credit top-ups to free-tier accounts and couples the conversion funnel with a streamlined Security Questionnaire (SQ) flow for teams showing enterprise intent. Hypothesis: Regular micro-allowances will increase habitual product usage and surface conversion intent; reducing SQ friction for engaged teams will shorten enterprise contract cycles and increase conversion rate.

Scope: 1) Implement backend credit schedule that grants configurable micro-credits (variants: 25, 75, 200 token-equivalent) on a weekly cadence for new free accounts for the first 8 weeks. 2) Track credit redemption patterns, session frequency, and prompt-level engagement. 3) Implement a contextual SQ prefill + templated question set that can be auto-sent to enterprise leads after a conversion trigger (usage threshold or upgrade intent). 4) Run A/B with control (no pulses) vs pulse variants and SQ streamlined vs standard SQ.

Success metrics (primary): 14-day active rate lift, trial-to-paid conversion within 30 days uplift, median time-to-enterprise-contract signed reduced. Secondary: credit redemption %, weekly session frequency, early churn reduction. Safety metrics: spike in low-quality/abusive usage, cost per converted customer, fraud indicators.

Measurement & instrumentation: Events to fire: credit_issued, credit_redeemed, session_start, conversion_intent, sq_sent, sq_completed, enterprise_signed. Dashboards: PLG Pulse dashboard (Metabase/Looker) with cohorts by pulse variant and source. Funnel to track conversion_time distribution. Tracking boards and target KPIs in Confluence.

Rollout plan: 1) Backend feature branch + opt-in flag; internal dogfood cohort (10% engineering/test orgs) for 1 week; 2) Canary: 5% of new signups for 2 weeks; 3) Ramp to 25% if no safety flags; 4) Full experiment for 8-week window, then analyze. SQ streamlining will be gated by an explicit trigger (e.g., account reaches 200k tokens usage or requests enterprise contract via sales touch).

Risks & trade-offs: - Additional credits increase short-term token cost; need guardrails and spend budget for experiment. - Fraud: attackers could create many accounts to harvest pulses — mitigation: rate limits, device/email heuristics, recaptcha, and require minimal activity prior to redemption. - SQ automations create compliance risk if misfilled — mitigation: legal/infosec signoff and audit log of prefills.

Dependencies & stakeholders: Product (Aisha, Jonah), Eng (runtime + billing), Design (Lucia Moreno), Security & Legal (Squad: Priya Nair), Sales/RevOps for enterprise handoff. Backend dependency: ENG-94213 (credit ledger + scheduler). Frontend: DES-3887 (new billing banner UI).

Artifacts & links: - Spec & measurement plan: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Pulse+Credits+Spec - Design mocks: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/Pulse-Credits-UI - Drive folder with experiment assets: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PulseCredits - GitHub prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pulse-credits/pull/27 - SQ template draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/SQ+Pulse+Template

Next steps: - Finalize variant sizes and guardrails (due 2026-03-18). - Eng spike to validate scheduler and cost accounting (ENG-94213, due 2026-03-24). - Security review of SQ template and auto-prefill flow (requested 2026-03-01). - Schedule canary cohort and monitoring alerts (SRE).
comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha: Initial spec posted. Hypothesis and metrics reviewed by PLG analytics. Added pulse size variants and weekly cadence.
2026-02-26 - Lucia Moreno (Design): Shared two design concepts — subtle in-console credit strip vs dedicated 'credit pulse' notification. Prefer banner with redeem CTA to avoid disrupting flows.

2026-03-01 - Priya Nair (Security): Reviewed SQ template draft. Identified three high-risk prefills (encryption, data residency, KMS). Requested audit logging and manual sign-off for any auto-submitted answers.
2026-03-04 - Jonah: Eng spike scheduled. Concern raised about cost attribution across free vs paid; asked billing to add experiment tag to usage records (ENG-94213).
2026-03-09 - Analytics: Prelim power calc indicates detectible lift if CR increases by 1.5pp; recommended sample size of ~6k new signups per arm over 8 weeks.
2026-03-12 - PM review: Decided to include a redemption-delay guard (require 24h of activity) to mitigate abuse. Also to cap weekly credit redemptions to prevent runaway spend.
2026-03-14 - Legal: Approved SQ template for pilot with clause to require customer attestation before final contract. Next action: integrate prefills with account audit log.
